- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 2-5% in next 5-7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1-2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >10% above forecast, sentiment was likely bullish; model was too cautious; increase next forecast by 1-3%.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often underestimates; add 1-2% to forecast for next 3-5 days.
- Avoid forecasting >15% above recent 7-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.80) and confirmed by 2+ consecutive positive sentiment days.
